messages:
maria: Heads-up — on the last canary we saw dashboard tile renders spike when prefetcher hits authz checks. CPU on query-side doubled for ~30s.
aj: saw that too, logs show a bunch of 403s from the authz-service and retries piling up :grimacing:
kevin: example logs: ```WARN tile_prefetcher.go:93 tenant=acme error=403 authz: missing perm
GET /v1/tiles?ids=[...] 403
```
anne: is prefetch running inline with the main render path or async? if inline we should bail fast
maria: currently inline for cold tiles to avoid flash. We added retry loop which now retries on 403 for 5s, that was dumb.
aj: +1 remove retry on 403, fallback to empty tile and record missing-perm metric
samir: tradeoff: users will see holes on first load. Could we lazily fetch after initial render and replace tile when available? that keeps SLO
kevin: propose: 1) stop retrying on 403 2) run prefetch async with a short deadline 3) add RBAC cache near the prefetcher (local TTL 30s) 4) gate cache warmups behind a tenant-rate token bucket
maria: sounds good. any perf concerns with local RBAC cache memory per-worker?
anne: memory negligible if we store only tenant IDs + bitmask. prefer 30s TTL to avoid staleness. We'll need a revocation path but OK for now.
aj: I'll open a small follow-up RFC for the interface changes (prefetcher -> authz cache API) and add migration plan. For immediate, I'll cut retry loop and roll canary
maria: thanks — canary window 15m, I'll watch dashboards and SLOs. @ops-bot schedule deploy 10m
ops-bot: deploy queued for service=console-prefetcher env=staging in 10m :rocket:
kevin: also let's add a metric 'prefetch.authz.403' and a histogram for prefetch latency so we can spot regressions
maria: agreed, assignable actions: aj remove retries, kevin add metrics, anne design RBAC cache shape, samir prototype async swap. Back in 24h for status.
